newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB down on Time Warner interactive threat.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB down on Time Warner interactive threat.

text.p: Shares in Rupert Murdoch's British Sky Broadcasting Plc dropped in early trade on Monday, hit by a report that Time Warner plans an offensive against satellite broadcasters with an interactive TV system in the U.S., dealers said.

The stock was down 9-1/2p at 556-1/2 by 0834 GMT in thin volume of just 5,390 shares. The Times newspaper reported Time Warner planned to roll out a system called Pegasus across the U.S. at a cost of some $5.0 billion, making it the most expensive project of its kind.

It said the project was being studied by British cable companies as a possible model for their own digital services including movies on demand, interactive games, home shopping and banking and ultimately high-speed access to the internet.

Last week BSkyB shares came under pressure amid rumours that Granada Group Plc was seeking to place all or part of its 11 percent stake in the satellite broadcaster ahead of its annual shareholders meeting this week.
The stock was also unsettled as Merrill Lynch cut the stock to "neutral" from "accumulate" after it reached a price target set by analysts at the brokerage.
